title: restore_learned_snapshot restores to a snapshot that carried no accuracy evidence
claim: On a fresh install the action restores (1 of 1 calls succeed) to the snapshot the first heartbeat took, whose recorded temperature_bias is None, discarding a heat-loss scale learned since (1.3 -> 1.0), where the documented rule admits only a snapshot captured with prediction accuracy in band and otherwise fails with an error.
mechanism: SnapshotRing.due() is True on an empty ring, so the first heartbeat takes a snapshot of the default learners with an accuracy summary that has no samples (temperature_bias None). best_restore() applies the band test only when bias is not None, so the unevidenced snapshot qualifies; undo_target() hands it to the service, and the drift watchdog's automatic rollback reads the same best_restore().

evidence.unit: restore calls that succeeded out of 1 (documented: 0, refused)
evidence.contention_note: two other finder seats on the box; counts are contention-immune

perturbation.change: best_restore skips a snapshot whose accuracy.temperature_bias is None (one-line 'if bias is None: continue'), in memory: f03_restore_unevidenced.py --perturb

metric_definition: restore_learned_snapshot calls that return without error on a fresh install after one cycle, and data['house_heat_loss_scale'] after one, with the scale moved to 1.3 since the snapshot
phenomenon_property: A snapshot enters the restore pool only when it carries an in-band accuracy measurement; a snapshot with no accuracy evidence never qualifies for the manual or the automatic rollback.
reproduction_steps: Set up a fresh entry and let one update cycle run
Call heatpump_optimizer.restore_learned_snapshot: it succeeds and the scale returns to 1.0 instead of the call failing
proposed_fix_scope: snapshots.SnapshotRing.best_restore: require a finite in-band temperature_bias (treat None as unqualified); the undo point keeps its own path.
